assays.assay_description: Wistar rats trained to self-administer 10% alcohol underwent extinction and were tested in a 1-hour FR1 relapse/reinstatement session. Psilocybin (0, 1, or 2.5 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered 4 hours before the session; active and inactive lever presses were recorded.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (1 and 2.5 mg/kg) or vehicle (0 mg/kg) were administered 4 hours before the relapse session.

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were trained to self-administer 10% alcohol and underwent extinction training prior to the test session, establishing prior apparatus exposure.

setup_restrain.evidence: Standard operant self-administration chambers; animals freely move and press levers.

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were ad libitum in home cages; standard operant chamber does not contain home-cage food during a 1-hour relapse session.

water_restriction.evidence: Water not accessible inside the operant chamber during the 1-hour session.

time_to_assay.evidence: Psilocybin ... were administered 4 hours before the relapse session.

sample_size.evidence: Repeated measures ANOVA reported as F[2,28] (3 dose groups). 'four Wistar batches (n = 32 each) ... fourth batch was used for operant self-administration following psilocybin treatment.'

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 and 2.5 mg/kg, i.p., 4 h pretreatment) significantly reduced active lever presses during cue-induced reinstatement in alcohol-dependent rats compared with vehicle, with similar reduction at both doses (no dose-response). Inactive lever responding was unaffected, indicating no sedative effect.
outcomes.statistics: Repeated measures ANOVA: dose effect F[2,28]=10.08, p<0.001; lever effect F[1,28]=77.69, p<0.001; dose × lever interaction F[2,28]=10.40, p<0.001. Post hoc: vehicle vs both doses p<0.001; 1 vs 2.5 mg/kg p=0.49.
outcomes.evidence: We observed a highly significant dose but no dose-response effect with similar reduction in relapse for alcohol with both doses of psilocybin as compared to the vehicle ... Inactive lever responding was unaffected by psilocybin treatment.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Active and inactive operant responses were recorded.

E8_food_water.evidence: Only alcohol delivered via lever; no food/water available.

D3_recording_days.evidence: One relapse session recorded for the psilocybin manipulation.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline recording reported within this psilocybin assay.

D5_followup.evidence: Test conducted 4 h after drug; no ≥24 h follow-up reported.

D6_circadian.evidence: Session was 1 hour, far less than 6 h.

judge_notes: Only the operant alcohol self-administration / cue-induced reinstatement session involved psilocybin administration to behaving rats; this is the single scorable behavioural assay.

Excluded: ASST and delay discounting (no psychedelic administered to those cohorts), gene expression / Grm2 RT-PCR (molecular, not behavioural), microdialysis (not behaviour-focused with psychedelic), FDG-PET (LY379268 used, not a psychedelic; PET is imaging-only without behavioural readout), viral mGluR2 manipulations (not psychedelic).
All three candidates converged on the same single assay; merged consistent scores. D2 set to 1 (15–60 min) based on explicit '1-hour session' text, overriding gptoss's <15 min score.
Sex set to 'male' (medium confidence) since explicit male statements appear and no female subjects are reported, though sex for the psilocybin Wistar batch is not directly stated.
